editorial.headline: Land Preparation: The Work Before Construction Begins
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers the ground-shaping, investigation and site-readiness work that allows construction and selected mining sites to proceed.
editorial.body:
Land preparation is the practical work of making a site ready for what follows. It includes clearing and conditioning construction land, removing scrub, excavating, cutting slopes, filling and levelling ground, digging trenches, and moving, crushing or blasting rock. The scope also reaches earthworks for roads, railways, airport runways, taxiways and parking areas, factories, power facilities, production facilities, buildings and other civil works. It is the work that turns an undeveloped or difficult site into ground capable of receiving construction.

The activity is broader than grading alone. It includes installing, moving and protecting utilities; conducting site tests through sondir and bore methods; drilling; material extraction; and field investigations or sampling for construction, geophysical, geological or similar purposes. It also includes construction-site drainage, agricultural or forestry land drying, preparation for nuclear-energy facilities, and preparation for mining sites other than oil and gas. Supporting preparation work is within the scope too, including temporary construction aids such as sheet piles, project signs, cable-installation culverts, offices, basecamps, site-management facilities, warehouses and project workshops.

Registration is open at Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar scale. Nationally, the activity is TERBUKA to PMA, with foreign ownership permitted up to 100%. That is a clear national position: a foreign investor is not confined to a minority stake under this activity. The practical distinction is between the substantial fieldwork described here and any assumptions an applicant might make from the construction work that comes after it; this activity is specifically about preparing the land and site conditions themselves.

Bali does not block PMA registration for this activity under its province-wide, permanent moratorium on all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI. At the Besar scale, the OSS risk is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi—Medium-High/High—so the activity falls outside that moratorium rather than being barred by it. In Bali, the activity sits outside the province-wide moratorium because its Large-scale OSS risk is Medium-High/High.
